title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། ཚད་མ། ནེ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 181)
shelf_note: Derge Tengyur Pramāṇa section volume Ne (vol. 181), authentic canonical Tibetan Buddhist epistemological treatise.

tr_errors_A.english: The phrase "from where would it be" means that what is not produced from incapacity is indeed produced
tr_errors_A.problem: Reverses the epistemological causal argument: the source states that an effect cannot arise from an incapable cause, whereas the English states that it is produced from incapacity.

tr_errors_A.english: Regarding the objection, "Is it not the case that from an intellect perceiving blue and so forth, an intellect perceiving yellow and so forth does not fail to arise?",
tr_errors_A.problem: Double negation misconstrued: converts the opponent's premise that yellow cognition does not arise from blue cognition into the assertion that it does not fail to arise.

pages.prefer_reason: Translation B is accurate, philosophically sound, and preserves the logical flow, whereas Translation A contains a serious reversal in the refutation based on causal incapacity.

book_verdict: Authentic folio of the Derge Tengyur Pramāṇa section with completely accurate OCR; Translation B provides an exceptionally faithful translation, while Translation A reverses the core causal logic.
